lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 142, for issue 140: a shortcut bound to Switch Focused Split View Pane now switches panes.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one forty-two, for issue one forty: a shortcut bound to Switch Focused Split View Pane now switches panes.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The action now tells GTK whether it used the key, through one new function and a new test.
lines.say: The action now tells G T K whether it used the key, through one new function and a new test.

lines.caption: In split view, you press F6, which you bound to Switch Focused Split View Pane.
lines.say: In split view, you press F six, which you bound to Switch Focused Split View Pane.

lines.caption: The new callback notes which pane is selected, then asks for the panes to switch.
The other pane becomes active, by the same code as before, and the title shows its folder.
The pane changed, so it returns TRUE, and GTK treats the key as handled and stops it there.
lines.say: The pane changed, so it returns true, and G T K treats the key as handled and stops it there.

lines.caption: Before this PR, the callback switched panes but returned no value, so GTK passed F6 on.
lines.say: Before this PR, the callback switched panes but returned no value, so G T K passed F six on.

lines.caption: The split view's own F6 binding then moved focus straight back, so nothing seemed to happen.
lines.say: The split view's own F six binding then moved focus straight back, so nothing seemed to happen.

lines.caption: With split view off, it returns FALSE, so F6 keeps its usual GTK meaning.
lines.say: With split view off, it returns false, so F six keeps its usual G T K meaning.

lines.caption: The action has no key of its own. On the owner's machine F6 was bound to it, and did nothing visible.
lines.say: The action has no key of its own. On the owner's machine F six was bound to it, and did nothing visible.

lines.caption: Every other action callback in the window returns TRUE when it uses a key. This one was the only exception.
lines.say: Every other action callback in the window returns true when it uses a key. This one was the only exception.

lines.caption: It returns TRUE only when the selected pane really changed, so a key that switches nothing goes on to GTK.
lines.say: It returns true only when the selected pane really changed, so a key that switches nothing goes on to G T K.

lines.caption: Which widget took F6 is read from the code; the test shows the net effect.
lines.say: Which widget took F six is read from the code; the test shows the net effect.

lines.caption: Returning FALSE whenever nothing switched was the choice the issue's Risks section suggested.
lines.say: Returning false whenever nothing switched was the choice the issue's Risks section suggested.

lines.caption: The new function is short: note the selected pane, switch, and say whether the pane changed.
Now the bound key moves to the other pane, and pressing it again comes back.
With split view off, GTK's own F6 runs, and Shift+F6 is unchanged.
lines.say: With split view off, G T K's own F six runs, and Shift F six is unchanged.

lines.caption: The PR changes one source file, adds one verify script, and adds this page and its narration.
To undo it, point the action back at the old function and remove the new one.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The test failed on main and passed with the fix. A later local build, with the review's changes, passed every test too.
The fix follows the issue's analysis, and has the same shape as the other action callbacks.
Running the test on main first shows the fix, not the test, made the difference.
Most checks ran on the fix as first written; the code with the review's callback change was built and tested later.
On main's code, 30 of 31 tests passed, and the new one failed: F6 changed nothing.
lines.say: On main's code, thirty of thirty-one tests passed, and the new one failed: F six changed nothing.

lines.caption: With the fix, the build passed without warnings, the packages installed, and 31 of 31 tests passed.
lines.say: With the fix, the build passed without warnings, the packages installed, and thirty-one of thirty-one tests passed.

lines.caption: The new test showed F6 moving to the right pane, and a second F6 coming back.
lines.say: The new test showed F six moving to the right pane, and a second F six coming back.

lines.caption: With split view off, the longer test checks that F6 still moves the focus to the side pane, and it passed.
lines.say: With split view off, the longer test checks that F six still moves the focus to the side pane, and it passed.

lines.caption: After a third F6, End and F2 renamed a file in the right pane, so the keyboard followed the switch.
lines.say: After a third F six, End and F two renamed a file in the right pane, so the keyboard followed the switch.

lines.caption: The review's callback change built without warnings, and all 31 tests passed on it.
lines.say: The review's callback change built without warnings, and all thirty-one tests passed on it.

lines.caption: CI's four builds all failed because Launchpad's PPA was unavailable, so CI has run no tests or screenshots yet.
A fresh review agent found no correctness problems; it only noted this page was missing.
CI's first review found three low findings, all fixed in one commit, and it reviews every later push the same way.
R1: the test now also presses F6 with split view off.
lines.say: R one: the test now also presses F six with split view off.

lines.caption: R2: it now checks the keyboard focus, not just the title, by renaming a file in the right pane.
lines.say: R two: it now checks the keyboard focus, not just the title, by renaming a file in the right pane.

lines.caption: R3: the callback now reports the key handled only when the pane changed. CI's own check doubted it, but it was fixed anyway.
lines.say: R three: the callback now reports the key handled only when the pane changed. C I's own check doubted it, but it was fixed anyway.

lines.caption: CI's second review found two more low findings.
R4: a fixed wait in the test could be flaky; CI fixed it itself, so the test now waits for the title.
lines.say: R four: a fixed wait in the test could be flaky; C I fixed it itself, so the test now waits for the title.

lines.caption: R5, about step comments in the test, was accepted: it wasn't confirmed, and other verify scripts use such comments too.
lines.say: R five, about step comments in the test, was accepted: it wasn't confirmed, and other verify scripts use such comments too.

lines.caption: A third review, of the commits since then, found one more low finding.
R6, about how CI's new wait in the test reports a timeout, was accepted: it wasn't confirmed, and it only affects a failing run.
lines.say: R six, about how C I's new wait in the test reports a timeout, was accepted: it wasn't confirmed, and it only affects a failing run.

lines.caption: F6 on the owner's own desktop, where the bug was reported, waits for the next build.
lines.say: F six on the owner's own desktop, where the bug was reported, waits for the next build.

lines.caption: The PR, the changes, CI's comments with the screenshots, the issue and CI's four runs are all linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one, so nothing is queued to build on it.
Upstream Thunar has the same bug; this PR fixes only this fork.
In short: the key you bind to switch panes in split view now does switch them.
